reference: GNU coreutils cksum invoked by name in the isolated reference PATH. Its POSIX CRC-32 mode and supported GNU digest modes are the independent behavioral oracle; reference status is checked before candidate parity is reported.
coverage: POSIX CRC-32 output for named files and stdin
Empty and binary inputs, including the byte count
Multiple files, stdin in an argument list, and -- for dash-leading names
All six documented digest algorithms, tagged and untagged formats, and digest stdin
Missing-file continuation and invalid algorithm/option errors
Explicit dash operands retain their name, including repeated EOF and NUL-delimited records.
Same-shell parser failures leave input unread and reset options for later invocations.
Missing/directory/closed-input failures retain failure status while later checksums work.
exclusions: GNU --check, --raw, --base64, --length, legacy sysv/bsd/crc32b modes, and algorithms outside the documented set
Version banner identity and exact diagnostic wording
Very large inputs beyond the harness fixture limits

cases.purpose: Compare POSIX CRC-32 and byte counts for the same small text input as a named file and as stdin; the named form must include the filename while stdin must omit it.
cases.script:
printf 'abc\n' > plain
cksum plain
cksum < plain

cases.purpose: Exercise the zero-byte boundary and non-text bytes so the CRC and reported byte count are checked independently of line-oriented input.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf '\000\377A\n' > binary
cksum empty binary
cksum < empty

cases.purpose: Check ordered output for multiple operands with stdin between two files, including a binary file payload.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > first
printf 'last\000byte' > last
printf 'stream\001bytes' | cksum first - last

cases.purpose: Verify that -- ends option parsing so a dash-leading relative filename is opened and printed as a filename.
Compare NUL-terminated checksum records for a filename containing a space and an empty file.
cases.script:
printf 'space name data\n' > 'space name'
: > empty
cksum --zero -- 'space name' empty

cases.purpose: Compare GNU digest output for every digest algorithm documented by this loadable against deterministic binary input.
cases.script:
printf 'digest\000payload\377\n' > payload
for alg in md5 sha1 sha224 sha256 sha384 sha512; do cksum --algorithm="$alg" payload; done

cases.purpose: Check default tagged and explicit --tag output, --untagged output, the documented '-' name for digest stdin, and NUL termination for an untagged digest record.
cases.script:
printf 'sha input\n' > payload
printf 'zero delimiter\n' > 'space name'
cksum -a sha256 payload
cksum --tag --algorithm sha256 payload
cksum --untagged --algorithm=sha256 payload
cksum --untagged -a sha256 < payload
cksum -z --untagged -a sha1 -- 'space name'

cases.purpose: Ensure a missing operand reports an error and sets failure status while a later readable file still produces its checksum.
cases.script:
printf 'readable\n' > present
if cksum absent present; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare failure status and nonempty diagnostics for an unsupported algorithm name.
Compare failure status and nonempty diagnostics for an unknown option.
Check output for a relative filename containing a newline, where escaping or raw-name handling can affect checksum record bytes.
Check Bash metadata only: cksum is a builtin and help output includes the documented POSIX CRC-32 summary.
cases.script:
type -t cksum
help cksum > help.txt
found=no
while IFS= read -r line; do case $line in *'POSIX CRC-32'*) found=yes ;; esac; done < help.txt
[[ $found == yes ]]
printf 'help summary present\n'

cases.purpose: An explicit stdin operand is named dash; default stdin omits its name. Repeated dash operands see EOF on the second read, and zero mode keeps exact record delimiters.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' | cksum -
printf 'abc' | cksum
printf 'A\000B' | cksum -z - -

cases.purpose: Repeated reads in one shell preserve descriptor ownership, observe EOF, accept a fresh redirection, and reset digest selection to CRC on a later call.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > plain
{ cksum - -; cksum; } < plain
cksum < plain
cksum -a sha256 plain
cksum plain

cases.purpose: Missing algorithm and unsupported algorithm errors return 1 before reading stdin; zero/digest options do not leak into a later same-shell invocation.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > plain
{
 rc=0; cksum -a || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
 printf 'missing-algorithm=%s\n' "$rc"
 rc=0; cksum -z --algorithm=not-a-real-algorithm || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
 printf 'unsupported=%s\n' "$rc"
 cksum
} < plain
cksum --untagged -a sha256 plain
cksum plain

cases.purpose: Missing operands and directory read errors continue to stdin and valid files; CRC and digest closed-input failures return 1 and leave later invocations usable.
cases.script:
mkdir folder
printf 'abc' > present
rc=0; cksum absent folder - present < present || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'operands=%s\n' "$rc"
rc=0; cksum <&- || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
rc=0; cksum -a sha256 <&- || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'closed-inputs-rejected\n'
cksum present
